DEEP FIELD — CHOSEN

Instrument Serif for display, Literata for reading, JetBrains Mono for meta and code. Ships in both renderings; prefers-color-scheme picks the default.

Still minimal-mistakes underneath: _sass overrides plus one custom header include. No fork.

TWO TIERS, NOT ONE FEED

209 posts you wrote; 25 curated link roundups. Notes get images and space; links get a compact dated strip in the second accent.

This replaces the {% unless %} in _layouts/posts.html that currently just hides the roundups from the archive.

THE LIGHT RENDERING, LESS MONOTONE

The greys carried no chroma, so colour only ever appeared as text on a flat field. Fixed three ways:

1. Surfaces tinted toward the lavender — ground #F4F3FA, surface #E9E7F6.
2. The hero now sits on a tinted band (#EFEDFA) so the page reads as zones rather than one sheet.
3. Pull quotes carry a filled panel — the tinted-panel treatment, specced on the Foundations page.

Both palettes with their counterpart renderings, the type ramps, and the pull-quote spec.

Roles stay fixed across light and dark — ground, surface, text, muted, accent, links accent — which is what lets one set of custom properties drive both.

The shared rule: one accent for your writing, a second for curated links, never mixed.

FIELD NOTES — NOT CHOSEN

Kept here rather than deleted. Warm paper identity in Newsreader and IBM Plex, both renderings.

Its archive layout is worth stealing even if the identity isn't — the year gutter and the collapsed links row work in either direction.

TOPICS WITHOUT A HEADLINE

Every card the same size, every tag the same weight, both lists alphabetical. Counts are shown but never drive order or scale — so they stay information rather than hierarchy.

No topic appears in the primary nav. A blog with no main subject shouldn't pretend to have one.

Dark only so far; the light rendering uses the same tokens.
